name: inspect_asset
description: Inspect exactly one project source asset. Library items with builtin:* or library:* IDs belong to browse_library. Every call returns source metadata; for AI-generated assets it also returns the original generation record: generationRecord.params mirrors the submit-call parameters with the FULL prompt/text (read_project and browse_assets only show a 160-character preview), so to regenerate or iterate, pass those params back into the matching submit tool. generationRecord.record "missing" means the original job record is gone (deleted source project or cross-project copy) and only the preview survives. Audio/video metadata may include transcript state and, when ASR is available, a preview of up to 60 characters plus segmentCount, but does not include transcript rows by default. transcript.readyForEditing=true is authoritative for transcript, Script, and caption work even when the source upload lifecycle is still processing or the cloud copy is unavailable. Request a uniform coarse video overview with sourceFrameCount, exact real frames with sourceTimesMs, transcript rows for source-time ranges with transcriptRangesMs, or frames and transcript together. sourceTimesMs and transcriptRangesMs always address original source-asset time, never timeline time. A coarse frame overview covers only sampled moments; to find every occurrence of a visual event, scan the source in bounded exact timestamps and refine candidate intervals without claiming unseen intervals were checked. Desktop and the built-in Web agent can resolve source frames through the current editor without cloud upload. Hosted external MCP and backend fallback require a cloud-readable copy. Images/SVGs are previewed inline unless includeImagePreview is false. Project-stored motion graphics, effects, and transitions return schema/defaults. Use browse_assets to find or compare multiple project source assets. Do not use this for placed timeline instances. Pass includeCode:true to include source code for code-backed assets.

assetId.description: Exactly one project source asset ID or unambiguous ID prefix. Use browse_assets to find and compare project assets. Library IDs (builtin:* or library:*) belong to browse_library.

includeCode.description: Include stored source code for effects and transitions. On the backend agent this does not return Motion Graphic source; use includeCodeFile:true for MGs.

includeImagePreview.description: For image/SVG metadata reads, set false to omit the automatic inline preview.

includeTimecode.description: For source-frame screenshots assembled by the editor, set false to omit the caption strip below each image. Exact source timestamps remain available in the returned metadata. Defaults to true.

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.

sourceFrameCount.description: Uniform coarse overview across most of the source duration, up to 25 frames. For a broad visual survey, batch 12-20 frames in one call, then use exact sourceTimesMs for details. It avoids the final 1-5 seconds for decoder safety and cannot prove that short visual events were absent; use exact sourceTimesMs to scan or refine specific intervals. Cannot be combined with sourceTimesMs.

sourceTimesMs.description: Exact timestamps in the original source asset, in milliseconds; these are not timeline times. Every timestamp must be before the known source duration. Cannot be combined with sourceFrameCount.

transcriptRangesMs.description: Request transcript text that overlaps these original source-asset ranges. This is the only input that requests transcript rows; omit it to receive only transcript state and, when available, a preview of up to 60 characters plus segmentCount in asset metadata. When provided, pass 1-6 ranges. Each range is [startMs, endMs), must have startMs < endMs, and must stay within the known source duration. The ranges may cover at most 120 seconds total; no context is added before or after them. Returned rows keep their own timestamps and may cross a requested boundary when they overlap it.

endMs.description: Exclusive end in original source-asset milliseconds.

startMs.description: Inclusive start in original source-asset milliseconds.
